saturation_note: Reached. The turn came after roughly 40 queries. Searches 45-50 were run explicitly as saturation checks across six deliberately different vocabularies, and four of the six returned zero new names: (1) 彩色电子纸 整机 厂家 Spectra 6 供应商 一台起订 - only Advantech and a sub-threshold M5Stack kit; (2) e-paper poster 31.5in buy one unit local push no cloud - zero new, all Good Display/Geniatech/E Ink storefronts; (3) 电子纸 广告机 厂家 开放API/HTTP接口/MQTT 局域网 - zero new; (4) 电子纸 智慧门牌 整机 厂商 苏州/杭州/宁波/青岛 - zero new, geographic slicing beyond the Shenzhen/Dongguan/Guangzhou/Dalian cluster is exhausted; (5) large e-paper 13in+ ODM China/Taiwan/Japan/Korea - one straggler (Qingdao Ansenke); (6) 墨水屏 大尺寸 生产企业 名录 排名 2026 - one straggler (Shenzhen Meidewei), everything else already recorded. Three independent English SEO round-ups (zhsunyco, jiclcd, armordigitalscreen) had already converged on the same core set, which was the first saturation signal. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: saturation was reached on the reachable web, not on the field. Three of the richest enumerable sources were blocked - the Touch Taiwan 101-partner exhibitor list (403), the epaperia 260-member database behind a search form, and every Alibaba/1688 product page (empty bodies). The true long tail is certainly larger than what is recorded here; I hit the limit of what could be fetched, not the limit of what exists.

leads_not_followed.lead: epaperia.com industry database at /Search.html - the alliance's 260+ member directory.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: I fetched the landing page and the council-member page, which together named about 25 companies. The searchable database behind /Search.html holds the other ~235. It is the definitive map of the Chinese long tail.

leads_not_followed.lead: Alibaba and 1688 product pages are unfetchable (empty bodies) and Zhihu returns 403.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Roughly 15 marketplace ODMs in this report rest on an AI aggregator's secondhand reading of Alibaba listings rather than the listings themselves. Price and MOQ figures for that tier should be re-verified by a human with a browser before anyone acts on them.

leads_not_followed.lead: Metoree's Japanese ranking of 26+ 電子ペーパー manufacturers returned 403.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Japan produced three genuinely new integrators (CREA, TEIDEC, StellarLink) from a single search. A full Japanese vendor list would likely yield several more, and Japanese vendors are unusually forthcoming about local connectivity (RJ-45, HDMI, USB).

leads_not_followed.lead: Guangdong Mingjinkang's 25.3in colour poster at USD 390-430 MOQ 1, reportedly RK3566-based.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: If real, it is a third of the price of any comparable unit and an Android SoC would likely permit ADB-based local pushing. This is the single highest-value item to verify with a direct quote.

leads_not_followed.lead: CREA's HDMI input on its 42in and 32in monochrome e-paper signage.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: HDMI on an EPD is nearly unheard of and would let an ordinary computer drive a 42in e-paper panel with no vendor software at all. Worth confirming directly with CREA, including whether the colour models have it.

leads_not_followed.lead: Good Display's ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U mainboard in the 31.5in DMPH315E6x, plus downloadable XTacepSetup and Smart EPD APP.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: An ESP32-S3 is fully documented and reflashable. This is the most plausible route to a genuinely open local-push 31.5in colour display. Someone should dump the firmware and see whether the WiFi update path is a plain HTTP endpoint.

leads_not_followed.lead: Agile Conversion Engine (ACE) middleware and its new Navori Labs CMS bridge.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: First middleware to make e-paper drivable from a mainstream CMS. Agile's country and corporate identity were not stated in E Ink's release and could not be established without guessing.

leads_not_followed.lead: AUO Display Plus / E Ink joint venture output and which brands it is building for.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: StellarLink's aecoPost is one confirmed badge. Identifying the rest would reveal how much of the 31.5in market is a single Taoyuan production line under different logos - important for judging whether vendor diversity is real or cosmetic.
A ~USD 1.2bn bet on a non-E-Ink reflective technology. Currently zero revenue and stalled, but it is the only credible path to breaking the film monopoly at scale. Worth a status check annually.

leads_not_followed.lead: 13.3in consumer art frames sold single-unit in the West: Huessen EPF1301 (B&H, Petra), Aluratek, InkPoster, eco4lifehome.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the only large colour e-paper products confirmed purchasable by an individual through normal retail with app/cloud sync. Their integration openness was never examined in this sweep because the brief pointed at Asian ODMs.

leads_not_followed.lead: Sharp EP-C251 (25.3in) and EP-421 (42in) individual spec pages.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Only the 13.3in EP-C131 page was fetched. The 25.3in colour model in particular may have better connectivity than the 13.3in, which lacks WiFi and LAN entirely.

leads_not_followed.lead: Shenzhen Gode Xinc's 超稳态液晶显示技术 (ultra-stable LCD).
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A reflective display route that is neither electrophoretic nor ChLCD, surfaced only in the alliance council list. Unexamined.

leads_not_followed.lead: Chinese government procurement records (中标公告) for e-paper bus-stop and signage deployments.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Tender awards name the actual winning integrators with prices, which is far harder evidence than marketplace listings. A Yangzhou e-paper bus-stop pilot surfaced in search but was not pursued.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the 42in class is E Ink's ED420TT1 panel in every case.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Sharp, CREA, DKE, Holitech, Good Display and ATZ all offer a 42in monochrome. If they are all the same panel, the apparent vendor diversity at 42in is one panel with six badges.
